plants.name: Lavandula angustifolia
plants.description: Rolling rows of slender silvery stems topped with dense spikes of fragrant violet-blue flowers. The blooms hum with bees and perfume the warm summer air across fields and cottage gardens.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late June through August, peaking in early to mid July
plants.location: Provence, France, and other Mediterranean-climate regions of Europe
plants.funFact: Lavender's name probably comes from the Latin 'lavare', meaning 'to wash'. Romans used it to scent their baths and laundry.

plants.name: Hydrangea macrophylla
plants.description: Big, rounded clusters of blossoms that look like pom-poms, in shades from blue to pink. They brighten shady garden corners and coastal hedgerows.
plants.bloomingSeason: Early summer through late summer, with a strong show in early July
plants.location: Gardens in the northeastern United States, the United Kingdom, and coastal Japan
plants.funFact: The flower color depends on soil chemistry. Acidic soil lets the plant take up aluminum, which turns the blooms blue, while alkaline soil gives pink flowers.

plants.name: Protea cynaroides
plants.description: A dramatic, bowl-shaped flower head with a crown of silky pink bracts around a downy center. It grows on the rugged fynbos slopes of the Southern Hemisphere, where it blooms through the cool winter.
plants.bloomingSeason: Peaks in late winter and spring, with flowering also found in mid-winter months such as July
plants.location: Fynbos of the Western Cape, South Africa
plants.funFact: The king protea is South Africa's national flower. It has evolved to survive wildfires, resprouting from underground stems after a burn.
